crates_created.name: oya-governance-tos-policy-kernel
crates_created.bnf_justification: oya-<microservice:foundry>-<bc:fitness-tos-policy>-<layer:kernel>; v4.1 conformant — extends the `oya-governance-*-kernel` family; layer=kernel: pure ToSAcknowledgment value types + pooling_policy_check decision function + pure-record audit event emission. New crate (not an extension of `oya-foundry-policy-kernel` which doesn't exist yet — only `oya-intelligence-policy-domain` does) per ICM scaffold-lock 01KRMC1M5Y99AMDZJB69JGT9QY.
crates_created.purpose: Gate pool-membership > 1 on a non-revoked per-(tenant, provider) ToS-ack. Emit EVT-PROVIDER-POOL-ROUTING audit-chain entry per routing decision with redacted account suffixes.
crates_created.linus_good_taste: ToS-ack is binary — present (a row with tenant_id, provider, version, accepted_at, accepted_by, evidence_hash) or absent. One predicate, one verdict, no 'we'll prompt later' branch.

symbols_shipped: PoolingPolicyVerdict::{Allow, Deny}, PoolingPolicyDenial::{ToSAckRequired, ToSAckRevoked, PoolSizeExceeded, BlocklistedDualUse}
ccproxy_parity: Net-new vs ccproxy-api — ccproxy ships no ToS-acknowledgment ledger and no audit-chain emission per routing decision. This IP closes both gaps.
open_items: Cedar policy file `foundry.pooling.cedar` deferred — kernel ships the Rust decision function; the cross-check property test against the Cedar evaluator wires in app layer when oya-policy-cedar-domain is available.
Operator-console onboarding wizard deferred — UI hand-off to a future `oya-foundry-console-tos-wizard` crate.
